nutshell: Most visible-infrared person ReID (VI-ReID) work only evaluates cross-modal matching (query in one modality, gallery entirely in the other), but real deployments have mixed galleries containing both modalities. MixER addresses this by decomposing a single backbone's features into a modality-erased component (for cross-modal matching) and a modality-related component (for same-modality discrimination) via orthogonal decomposition, adversarial modality-confusion, and a doubled identity-modality label space, then fuses both at inference for mixed-modal galleries.
contributions: Formalizes four new, more realistic mixed-modal evaluation settings (Mix, Mix-Camera, Mix-Camera-ID, Mix-ID) that progressively remove same-modality/same-camera positives from the gallery, explicitly critiquing a prior mixed-modal setting (Mix-P from Liu et al.) as too easy to be discriminative between methods.

MixER: a single-backbone method that splits features into modality-erased (z^e, for cross-modal matching) and modality-related (z^r, for intra-modal refinement) via orthogonal-decomposition loss, a GRL-based modality-confusion loss, and a doubled label space (y'=2y for visible, 2y+1 for infrared) that lets one cross-entropy loss jointly encode identity and modality without a separate classifier head.

Shows the modality-erased/-related learning losses can be grafted onto other existing VI-ReID backbones (DDAG, MPANet, DEEN, SGEIL, SAAI, IDKL) as a plug-in, improving their mixed- and cross-modal performance without added inference-time cost (Table 3).
State-of-the-art results across SYSU-MM01, RegDB, and LLCM in both the new mixed-modal settings and standard cross-modal settings, using a single backbone rather than separate models per setting.
deficiencies: The modality-related-only ablation (MixER(R)) - one of the two core components the paper's method is built around - collapses catastrophically outside its intended use: on SYSU-MM01 cross-modal 'All Search' it scores 1.19% R1 / 3.61% mAP (versus ~70-75% for every other method in the table), and Mix-ID mAP is 0.99%. The paper only softens this as 'modality-related features perform less effectively' in cross-modal settings, which understates a near-total collapse rather than a modest weakness.

The headline 'more comprehensive mixed-modal evaluation' contribution only fully applies to SYSU-MM01 - RegDB and LLCM have one camera per modality, so Mix-Camera and Mix-Camera-ID (2 of the paper's 4 new settings) are inapplicable there, leaving only Mix and Mix-ID reported for 2 of the 3 benchmarked datasets.

MixER is built directly on top of the SAAI backbone/hyperparameters ('following [9]', same 180-epoch schedule, same ResNet50), and the paper never ablates a different backbone choice - it's unclear how much of the reported gain is attributable to the proposed modality-erased/-related learning versus starting from an already-strong SAAI baseline.

In the loss ablation (Table 5), adding the final fusion loss L_f is described as achieving 'optimal results across all metrics,' but the actual Cross-Modal gain from adding it is negligible (R1 73.40→73.43, mAP 70.87→70.92) even though Mix-Cam-ID jumps substantially (84.64→87.56 R1) - the improvement is concentrated in the mixed-modal metrics, not evenly 'across all metrics' as stated.
notable: The doubled label space trick (y'=2y for visible identities, y'=2y+1 for infrared) is a simple, reusable way to make a single cross-entropy loss jointly discriminate identity and modality without adding a separate classifier head or auxiliary loss term - useful for other multi-modal ID-plus-attribute learning setups beyond VI-ReID. Also notable: this paper is itself an extension of the same first author's BMVC2023 'Bidirectional Multi-Step Domain Generalization' (BMDG) VI-ReID paper already summarized earlier in this batch (ref [3] here) - the two papers address related but distinct problems (domain generalization vs. mixed-modal galleries) from the same research group.
